title: Customer 207's notes
scenario: A software company uses agent memory in three places: a support agent with the Claude memory tool, a sales assistant on the OpenAI Agents SDK, and a coding agent in its main repo. You audit all three (exhibit).
exhibit:
1) SUPPORT AGENT  (Claude API + memory tool)
   storage: one folder per customer, /memories/<customer_id>/
   handler: real_path = "/data" + input.path   (no other checks)
   log 10-02  view    /memories/c_481/../c_207/notes.md
              -> returned customer c_207's notes to customer c_481
   log 10-03  create  /memories/c_481/payment.md
              text: "card 4111 1111 1111 1111, exp 09/28"

2) SALES ASSISTANT  (OpenAI Agents SDK, one SQLiteSession per user)
   user u_88: 14 months of chat, 9,400 stored items
   each run loads all items; cost per reply up 6x since March

3) MAIN REPO  (coding agent)
   CLAUDE.md: 640 lines
   line 12:  Use npm for installs.
   line 418: Use Bun. Never use npm.

questions.prompt: How should the support agent's handler stop the 10-02 leak?

options.text: Tell Claude in the system prompt to stay inside its own folder and never use `../` paths.
options.explanation: A prompt asks; it does not enforce. A crafted path can still reach the handler, which must check it.

options.text: Resolve every path to its canonical form and reject any that leaves the allowed folder.
options.explanation: Right. The memory tool docs say to validate every path in every command, resolve it to its canonical form and reject traversal sequences like `../`.

options.text: Rename the folders to random ids so they are hard to guess, and hide the base path.
options.explanation: Hidden names do not fix the hole. Any path with `../` still escapes the folder once a name is known.

options.text: Turn on memory expiration so old notes are deleted.
options.explanation: Expiration limits how long files live. It does not stop a bad path from reading another folder today.

questions.prompt: On 10-03, a card number was written to memory. What do the memory tool docs recommend?

options.text: Nothing: Claude refuses to write sensitive data, so this cannot happen in a real run.
options.explanation: The docs say Claude usually refuses. Usually is not always, and the log shows it happened.

options.text: Encrypt the folder, then keep storing card numbers in memory for later sessions.
options.explanation: Encryption protects storage at rest, but the card number would still be read back into the context later.

options.text: Turn off the memory tool for all customers.
options.explanation: That removes the feature instead of fixing the write path. The docs give a narrower fix.

options.text: Add validation in the handler that strips sensitive data before it writes the file.
options.explanation: Right. For stronger guarantees than Claude's usual refusal, the docs say to strip sensitive data before your handler writes.

questions.prompt: The sales assistant loads 9,400 items each run. Which change fits the OpenAI Agents SDK docs?

options.text: Set `SessionSettings(limit=N)` so each run retrieves only the latest N items.
options.explanation: Right. The default, `limit=None`, retrieves all session items. A limit caps retrieval without changing what the session stores.

options.text: Keep the session and also pass `previous_response_id` on each run, to link the turns.
options.explanation: A session cannot be combined with `previous_response_id` in the same run, and mixing both can duplicate context.

options.text: Delete the session after every reply, so each run starts empty.
options.explanation: That fixes cost by removing memory completely. The user would lose the conversation they came back for.

options.text: Move the 9,400 items into the agent's instructions.
options.explanation: That loads the same tokens on every run, in a place that is even harder to trim.

questions.prompt: The coding agent sometimes uses npm and sometimes Bun. What do the Claude Code docs point to?

options.text: A model with a bigger context window, so all 640 lines fit.
options.explanation: The lines already load. The problems are length, which reduces adherence, and two rules that conflict.

options.text: Repeat line 418 three times so it wins.
options.explanation: Repetition does not remove the conflict. The docs say to review the files and remove outdated or conflicting instructions.

options.text: Delete line 12 and cut the file below 200 lines.
options.explanation: Right. With contradicting instructions Claude may pick one arbitrarily, and files over 200 lines consume more context and reduce adherence.

options.text: Move all 640 lines into auto memory instead.
options.explanation: Auto memory is for notes Claude writes itself, and only its first 200 lines or 25KB load per session.
